correctness.rationale: I independently enumerated the loopless face family, rebuilt the ordinary lexicographic acyclic matching, verified acyclicity by a full sort, evaluated the signed gradient-path boundary, and computed its exact Smith form. The Morse CW complex has one vertex, 132 four-cells, 312 five-cells and no other cells. The 132-by-312 attaching matrix has 131 unit Smith entries and one zero. Its four-skeleton is a wedge of 4-spheres, and Hurewicz identifies its pi_4 with the integral degree lattice. Homotopy equivalences of the source wedge of attaching spheres and of the skeleton realize the two integral basis changes in the homotopy cofiber. Thus 131 identity attachments can be removed, leaving exactly one 4-sphere and 181 5-spheres. Neither the cell counts nor a homology computation on an arbitrary 6-dimensional complex alone substitutes for this argument.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: If one takes the table statement as cited, the complex is 3-connected by Hurewicz. Represent the H_4 generator by S^4, giving an isomorphism on pi_4. The mapping-cylinder pair is then 4-connected, and relative Hurewicz and the two exact sequences give surjectivity pi_5 -> H_5. Realizing a basis of H_5 produces a homology equivalence from the stated wedge, hence a homotopy equivalence by simple connectivity. This supplies a standard deduction in addition to the independently verified direct prior coverage.
